# Dynadot
> Dynadot is an ICANN-accredited domain registrar offering domain registration, aftermarket services, DNS, email, website tools, and security products for individuals, businesses, and **domain investors** worldwide.

## Important notes
- ICANN-accredited registrar since 2002
- Built for domain investors with bulk and portfolio management tools
- Integrated aftermarket, auctions, and backorder systems for domain investing workflows
- API access for automation and large-scale domain management

## Domains
- [Domain Search](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/search): Search and register available domain names
- [AI Domain Search](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/ai-search): AI-assisted domain name discovery
- [Bulk Domain Search](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/bulk-search): Search and register domains in bulk
- [Advanced Domain Search](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/advanced-search): Filtered domain search with advanced options
- [IDN Search](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/idn-search): Search internationalized domain names
- [Domain Transfer](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/transfer): Transfer domains to Dynadot
- [Bulk Domain Transfer](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/bulk-transfer): Transfer multiple domains at once
- [Domain Prices](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/prices): TLD pricing for registration, renewal, and transfer
- [Domain Sales](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/sales): Discounted and promotional domain pricing
- [WHOIS Lookup](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/whois): Lookup domain ownership and registration details
- [Domain Suggestion Tool](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/suggestion-tool): Generate domain name ideas
- [Grace Deletion](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/grace-deletion): Delete domains during the grace period
- [Domain Security](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/security): Domain protection and security features
- [Domain API](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/api): Programmatic access to domain registrations, transfers, renewals, and general domain management

## Representative TLDs 
- [.COM Domains](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/com): Register and manage .com domains. Find .com domains prices, requirements, and other specifications.
- [.NET Domains](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/net): Register and manage .net domains. Find .net domains prices, requirements, and other specifications.
- [.ORG Domains](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/org): Register and manage .org domains. Find .org domains prices, requirements, and other specifications.
- [.IO Domains](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/io): Register and manage .io domains. Find .io domains prices, requirements, and other specifications.
- [.XYZ Domains](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/xyz): Register and manage .xyz domains. Find .xyz domains prices, requirements, and other specifications.

## Aftermarket
- [Aftermarket Search](https://www.dynadot.com/market/search): Search domains in all of Dynadot's aftermarket 
- [All Domain Auctions](https://www.dynadot.com/market/all-domain-auctions): Browse all live domain auctions
- [Expired Auctions](https://www.dynadot.com/market/auction): Browse all live Dynadot expired domain auctions
- [Registry Auctions](https://www.dynadot.com/market/registry-expired-auction): Browse registry-level expired auctions
- [Last Chance Auctions](https://www.dynadot.com/market/last-chance-auction): Final auction stage for expired domains not successfully acquired in other auctions
- [Expired Closeout](https://www.dynadot.com/market/expired-closeout): Fixed-price expired domains
- [User Listings](https://www.dynadot.com/market/user-listings): Domains for sale listed by users
- [User Auctions](https://www.dynadot.com/market/user-auction): Domain auctions created by users
- [Backorder](https://www.dynadot.com/market/backorder): Place backorders on expiring domains
- [Backorder Auctions](https://www.dynadot.com/market/backorder-auction): Auctions triggered by multiple backorders
- [Buy Domains](https://www.dynadot.com/market/buy-domains): Purchase domains via brokerage
- [Sell Domains](https://www.dynadot.com/market/sell-domains): Get a broker to help sell domains
- [Domain Appraisal](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/appraisal): Automated domain valuation tool using AI

## Tools
- [Website Builder](https://www.dynadot.com/website-builder): Build websites without coding
- [Email Hosting](https://www.dynadot.com/email): Domain-based email hosting
- [Logo Builder](https://www.dynadot.com/logo-builder): Create logos for your brand
- [SSL Certificates](https://www.dynadot.com/ssl): SSL certificates for website security
- [Reseller Program](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/reseller-program): Resell domains and services
- [Trademark Search](https://www.dynadot.com/free-uspto-trademark-search): Search US trademarks

## Resources
- [Dynadot Blog](https://www.dynadot.com/blog): Articles and updates on domains and internet trends
- [Newsletters](https://www.dynadot.com/market/newsletter): Get marketplace and Dynadot updates through their newsletter
- [Payment Options](https://www.dynadot.com/payment-options): Supported Dynadot payment methods and limitations 
- [Prepay](https://www.dynadot.com/prepay): Preload account balance by using Dynadot prepay
- [Domain Name Basics Guide](https://www.dynadot.com/domain/beginners-guide): Introduction to domain names
- [Domain Investing Guide](https://www.dynadot.com/domain-investing-guide): Guide to buying and selling domains
- [How to Buy Domains](https://www.dynadot.com/resources/how-to-buy-domains): Domain purchasing guide
- [How to Sell Domains](https://www.dynadot.com/resources/how-to-sell-domains): Domain selling guide
- [Affiliate Program](https://www.dynadot.com/affiliate): Earn commissions by referring users

## Support
- [Help Center](https://www.dynadot.com/help): Documentation and FAQs
- [Forums](https://www.dynadot.com/forums): Community discussions
- [Contact Support](https://www.dynadot.com/community/contact): Contact Dynadot support
- [Report Abuse](https://www.dynadot.com/report-abuse): Report abusive or illegal domain activity 

## Company
- [About Dynadot](https://www.dynadot.com/community/about-us): Company background and mission
- [Events](https://www.dynadot.com/community/events): Dynadot events and community activities
- [Refer a Friend](https://www.dynadot.com/community/refer-a-friend): Referral program to earn account credit
- [Terms of Use](https://www.dynadot.com/terms-of-use): Legal terms governing services

long-term usability, and the rules of the specific TLD (top-level domain) you are selecting. A domain name is a long-term digital asset that affects brand credibility, search visibility, and resale value. Consider the following: Branding & memorability: Short, clear, and easy-to-spell names perform better in marketing and reduce user friction. Trademark risk: Check for existing trademarks to avoid legal disputes, forced transfers, or rebranding costs. TLD rules: A TLD (the extension such as .com, .net, or .ai) may have eligibility, renewal, or pricing requirements set by the registry (the organization that operates the extension). Renewal costs: Some domains have higher renewal fees than initial registration prices. Long-term strategy: Determine whether the domain is for active use, brand protection, SEO positioning, or investment resale. Understanding how a registrar (the company through which you register domains) manages renewals, transfers, DNS settings, and privacy options is also important before committing to registration. If you have any questions or concerns, please do not hesitate to reach out to our support team, either at info@dynadot.com or via chat."}},{"@id":"https://www.dynadot.com/#/schema/question/7bf18ba","@type":"Question","inLanguage":"en","name":"How do I register a domain name?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"To register a domain name with Dynadot, follow these steps: 1. Visit the Domain Name Search page. 2. Enter your desired domain name into the search bar to check availability. 3. Click the shopping cart icon next to the available domain to add it to your cart. 4. Open the cart and select \"View Cart\" to review your selection. Note: Domain privacy is automatically included for eligible TLDs unless you have customized your default privacy settings. 5. Click \"Checkout\" and complete the purchase by following the steps. Once your order is processed, you will receive a confirmation email, and the domain will be registered to your Dynadot account."}},{"@id":"https://www.dynadot.com/#/schema/question/2ab6a5a","@type":"Question","inLanguage":"en","name":"How much does a domain name cost?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Domain name prices vary by extension (TLD) and transaction type: registration, renewal, or transfer. You can view the full pricing list for your desired domain extension on Dynadot’s pricing pages to see the current costs."}},{"@id":"https://www.dynadot.com/#/schema/question/5cbe430","@type":"Question","inLanguage":"en","name":"What's included with domain registration?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"When you register a domain with Dynadot, with your full domain ownership rights you get access to a variety of free tools and features to enhance your domain experience: Free logo builder Free email address Free website builder Free domain privacy (for eligible TLDs) Free DNS management Domain forwarding Full API access Comprehensive domain management tools These features are available with every domain registration, making it easy to manage and personalize your domain right from your Dynadot account."}},{"@id":"https://www.dynadot.com/#/schema/question/70a6710","@type":"Question","inLanguage":"en","name":"What payment methods does Dynadot support?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Dynadot supports a wide range of payment options, including: Credit/debit cards, PayPal, Skrill, Alipay, Payoneer, eCash, Bank Wire, Money Orders, Cashier’s and Personal Checks, Bank Transfers, Apple Pay, UnionPay, Direct Debit (Checking Account), Crypto, iDEAL, Google Pay, Mercado Pago, Wise. Payments can be made in multiple currencies, including USD, GBP, EUR, CNY, CAD, MXN, BRL, INR, IDR, and AUD. Additionally, you can use account credit for orders."}},{"@id":"https://www.dynadot.com/#/schema/question/f5047eb","@type":"Question","inLanguage":"en","name":"Is there a way to register several domains at the same time?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes! Dynadot’s bulk domain search tool allows you to search for and register multiple domains simultaneously. Simply enter each domain separated by a comma or space in the search box, run the search, and add the available domains to your cart for registration."}},{"@id":"https://www.dynadot.com/#/schema/question/0d190c1","@type":"Question","inLanguage":"en","name":"What happens after I register a domain?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"After registering a domain with Dynadot, you will: 1. Receive a confirmation email. 2. See the domain in your Dynadot account control panel. 3. Be able to set up DNS records, email forwarding, domain forwarding, a website, a custom email address, and other related services."}},{"@id":"https://www.dynadot.com/#/schema/question/63221e7","@type":"Question","inLanguage":"en","name":"How long does it take for a new domain name to be active after registering it?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"A newly registered domain name typically becomes active and usable within 0 to 48 hours after registration, although most are active within a few hours. This can vary by TLD."}},{"@id":"https://www.dynadot.com/#/schema/question/368798b","@type":"Question","inLanguage":"en","name":"How do I access and manage my domain settings once it’s registered?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Dynadot provides a centralized and secure domain management platform that makes managing your domains simple and efficient. Key features include: Smart Folders: Organize domains into folders for easy access and apply settings like Whois privacy or DNS configurations. Domain Default Settings: Set default options for new domains, including preferences specific to TLDs. Bulk Domain Adjustments: Update multiple domains at once to save time. Filtering: Quickly locate and manage specific domains using built-in filters. All of these tools are available through Dynadot’s user-friendly control panel, designed to support both small and large domain portfolios."}},{"@id":"https://www.dynadot.com/#/schema/question/5c4cc84","@type":"Question","inLanguage":"en","name":"Do you offer domain privacy protection?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes, Dynadot offers two domain privacy options: Partial privacy: Hides all personal information except your name. Full privacy: Hides all personal information, including your name. Domain privacy is added automatically with your domain registration, unless you change that in your privacy settings. Most top-level domains (TLDs) support privacy protection, but some TLDs don't support privacy protection due to registry restrictions."}},{"@id":"https://www.dynadot.com/#/schema/question/fe2c9d0","@type":"Question","inLanguage":"en","name":"If I register a domain, do I have to put my real name/address in Whois?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes, accurate registrant information is required when registering a domain. Providing false contact details can violate registration agreements and may lead to suspension or loss of the domain. Whois is the public record of domain ownership information required by ICANN (the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers). However: Most TLDs support domain privacy, which replaces your public contact details with proxy information. The registrar retains your verified real information internally. Privacy does not eliminate legal obligations or prevent court-ordered disclosures. Accurate ownership records are essential for transfers, dispute resolution, and asset verification during resale transactions."}},{"@id":"https://www.dynadot.com/#/schema/question/ad1990b","@type":"Question","inLanguage":"en","name":"What happens if I forget to renew my domain?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"If you forget to renew your domain, it typically enters a grace period during which you can renew it at the standard renewal price, but timelines vary by TLD. Failing to renew within that period can result in deletion, auction, or permanent loss. Most domains follow this lifecycle: 1. Expiration Date – The domain stops resolving if not renewed. 2. Grace Renewal Period (often up to 30 days, depending on the registry) – Renewal at regular cost is usually still possible. 3. Redemption Period – The domain may require a higher restoration fee. 4. Pending Delete Period – Final countdown before the domain is released to the public. 5. Public Re-registration – If not purchased, it becomes available to anyone. Some TLDs have shorter timelines or different policies. For investors, expired domains can attract competitive bidding due to traffic history, backlinks, or brandability, increasing reacquisition costs. Enabling auto-renew and maintaining valid payment methods reduces asset loss risk."}},{"@id":"https://www.dynadot.com/#/schema/question/7a77a94","@type":"Question","inLanguage":"en","name":"Can I transfer my existing domain to Dynadot?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes, you can transfer your domain to Dynadot! Here's how: 1. Before you start: Ensure your domain is at least 60 days old and unlocked. Obtain the authorization code from your current registrar. We recommend initiating the transfer at least two weeks before the domain's expiration. 2. Start the transfer: Visit our domain transfer page, enter your domain and authorization code, and then click Transfer. The domain is added to your cart and you can proceed to checkout. 3. After completion: You'll receive email updates as the transfer progresses, including confirmation and completion emails. One year is usually added to your domain's expiration date upon transfer, with some exceptions."}},{"@id":"https://www.dynadot.com/#/schema/question/6ead022","@type":"Question","inLanguage":"en","name":"Why is my personal website offline?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"A website can go offline due to DNS misconfiguration, domain expiration, hosting issues, or registry suspension. The cause is usually technical rather than permanent. Common reasons include: DNS Propagation Delay: After updating name servers or DNS records (Domain Name System settings that direct traffic to your hosting server), changes can take 5 minutes to 48 hours to fully propagate globally. Incorrect DNS Records: Mistyped A, AAAA, CNAME, or MX records can prevent resolution. Hosting Configuration Errors: The domain may not be properly linked to your hosting account. Domain Expiration: An expired domain stops resolving until renewed. Registry or Compliance Suspension: Domains may be suspended for policy violations, inaccurate contact data, or abuse reports. If DNS is correctly configured and the domain is active, the issue may be server-side rather than registrar-related. Checking DNS records, expiration status, and hosting configuration typically identifies the root cause. If you aren't sure, please contact our team at either info@dynadot.com or via Chat, and we will be happy to take a look."}},{"@id":"https://www.dynadot.com/#/schema/service/663b811","@type":"Service","areaServed":"CN","name":"域名注册服务","serviceType":"Domain Registration","provider":{"@id":"https://www.dynadot.com/entity/organization/dynadot"}}]}</script>

Most top-level domains (TLDs) support privacy protection, <!--[--><a href="/help/question/domain-privacy-not-allowed" class="">but some TLDs don't support privacy protection</a><!--]--> due to registry restrictions.</p><!--]--></div><!--]--></div></div></div><div class="dyna-collapse-item" data-v-1eda74d4><summary id="dyna-collapse-head-whois" class="dyna-collapse-item__header" tabindex="0" type="button"><span class="dyna-collapse-item__title"><!--[--><h3 class="faq-question py-5 text-lg font-semibold text-on-surface" data-v-1eda74d4>If I register a domain, do I have to put my real name/address in Whois?</h3><!--]--></span><!--[--><i class="text-xl leading-none text-on-surface fa-regular fa-circle-plus" data-v-1eda74d4></i><!--]--></summary><div id="dyna-collapse-content-whois" role="region" class="dyna-collapse-item__wrap" aria-hidden="true" aria-labelledby="dyna-collapse-head-whois" style="display:none;"><div class="dyna-collapse-item__content"><!--[--><div class="faqs-answer flex flex-col gap-4 font-switzer text-base text-on-surface" data-v-1eda74d4><!--[--><p>Yes, accurate registrant information is required when registering a domain. Providing false contact details can violate registration agreements and may lead to suspension or loss of the domain.</p><p>Whois is the public record of domain ownership information required by ICANN (the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers). However:</p><ul><li>Most TLDs support <!--[--><a href="/help/question/full-partial-domain-privacy" class="">domain privacy</a><!--]-->, which replaces your public contact details with proxy information.</li><li>The registrar retains your verified real information internally.</li><li>Privacy does not eliminate legal obligations or prevent court-ordered disclosures.</li></ul><p>Accurate ownership records are essential for transfers, dispute resolution, and asset verification during resale transactions.</p><!--]--></div><!--]--></div></div></div><div class="dyna-collapse-item" data-v-1eda74d4><summary id="dyna-collapse-head-forget-renew-domain" class="dyna-collapse-item__header" tabindex="0" type="button"><span class="dyna-collapse-item__title"><!--[--><h3 class="faq-question py-5 text-lg font-semibold text-on-surface" data-v-1eda74d4>What happens if I forget to renew my domain?</h3><!--]--></span><!--[--><i class="text-xl leading-none text-on-surface fa-regular fa-circle-plus" data-v-1eda74d4></i><!--]--></summary><div id="dyna-collapse-content-forget-renew-domain" role="region" class="dyna-collapse-item__wrap" aria-hidden="true" aria-labelledby="dyna-collapse-head-forget-renew-domain" style="display:none;"><div class="dyna-collapse-item__content"><!--[--><div class="faqs-answer flex flex-col gap-4 font-switzer text-base text-on-surface" data-v-1eda74d4><!--[--><p>If you forget to renew your domain, it typically enters a grace period during which you can renew it at the standard renewal price, but timelines vary by TLD. Failing to renew within that period can result in deletion, auction, or permanent loss.</p><p>Most domains follow this lifecycle:</p><ol><li>Expiration Date - The domain stops resolving if not renewed.</li><li>Grace Renewal Period (often up to 30 days, depending on the registry) - Renewal at regular cost is usually still possible.</li><li>Redemption Period - The domain may require a higher restoration fee.</li><li>Pending Delete Period - Final countdown before the domain is released to the public.</li><li>Public Re-registration - If not purchased, it becomes available to anyone.</li></ol><p>Some TLDs have shorter timelines or different policies. For investors, expired domains can attract competitive bidding due to traffic history, backlinks, or brandability, increasing reacquisition costs. Enabling auto-renew and maintaining valid payment methods reduces asset loss risk.</p><!--]--></div><!--]--></div></div></div><div class="dyna-collapse-item" data-v-1eda74d4><summary id="dyna-collapse-head-transfer-existing-domain" class="dyna-collapse-item__header" tabindex="0" type="button"><span class="dyna-collapse-item__title"><!--[--><h3 class="faq-question py-5 text-lg font-semibold text-on-surface" data-v-1eda74d4>Can I transfer my existing domain to Dynadot?</h3><!--]--></span><!--[--><i class="text-xl leading-none text-on-surface fa-regular fa-circle-plus" data-v-1eda74d4></i><!--]--></summary><div id="dyna-collapse-content-transfer-existing-domain" role="region" class="dyna-collapse-item__wrap" aria-hidden="true" aria-labelledby="dyna-collapse-head-transfer-existing-domain" style="display:none;"><div class="dyna-collapse-item__content"><!--[--><div class="faqs-answer flex flex-col gap-4 font-switzer text-base text-on-surface" data-v-1eda74d4><!--[--><p>Yes, you can transfer your domain to Dynadot! Here's how:</p><ol><li>Before you start: Ensure your domain is at least 60 days old and unlocked. The cause is usually technical rather than permanent.</p><p>Common reasons include:</p><ul><li>DNS Propagation Delay: After updating name servers or DNS records (Domain Name System settings that direct traffic to your hosting server), changes can take 5 minutes to 48 hours to fully propagate globally.</li><li>Incorrect DNS Records: Mistyped A, AAAA, CNAME, or MX records can prevent resolution.</li><li>Hosting Configuration Errors: The domain may not be properly linked to your hosting account.</li><li>Domain Expiration: An expired domain stops resolving until renewed.</li><li>Registry or Compliance Suspension: Domains may be suspended for policy violations, inaccurate contact data, or abuse reports.</li></ul><p>If DNS is correctly configured and the domain is active, the issue may be server-side rather than registrar-related. Checking DNS records, expiration status, and hosting configuration typically identifies the root cause. A domain name is a long-term digital asset that affects brand credibility, search visibility, and resale value. Consider the following: Branding & memorability: Short, clear, and easy-to-spell names perform better in marketing and reduce user friction. Trademark risk: Check for existing trademarks to avoid legal disputes, forced transfers, or rebranding costs. TLD rules: A TLD (the extension such as .com, .net, or .ai) may have eligibility, renewal, or pricing requirements set by the registry (the organization that operates the extension). Renewal costs: Some domains have higher renewal fees than initial registration prices. Long-term strategy: Determine whether the domain is for active use, brand protection, SEO positioning, or investment resale. Understanding how a registrar (the company through which you register domains) manages renewals, transfers, DNS settings, and privacy options is also important before committing to registration. This can vary by TLD.":1710,"How do I access and manage my domain settings once it’s registered?":1711,"Dynadot provides a centralized and secure domain management platform that makes managing your domains simple and efficient. All of these tools are available through Dynadot’s user-friendly control panel, designed to support both small and large domain portfolios.":1712,"Do you offer domain privacy protection?":1713,"Yes, Dynadot offers two domain privacy options: Partial privacy: Hides all personal information except your name. Full privacy: Hides all personal information, including your name. Domain privacy is added automatically with your domain registration, unless you change that in your privacy settings. Most top-level domains (TLDs) support privacy protection, but some TLDs don't support privacy protection due to registry restrictions.":1714,"If I register a domain, do I have to put my real name/address in Whois?":1715,"Yes, accurate registrant information is required when registering a domain. Providing false contact details can violate registration agreements and may lead to suspension or loss of the domain. Whois is the public record of domain ownership information required by ICANN (the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers). However: Most TLDs support domain privacy, which replaces your public contact details with proxy information. The registrar retains your verified real information internally. Privacy does not eliminate legal obligations or prevent court-ordered disclosures. Accurate ownership records are essential for transfers, dispute resolution, and asset verification during resale transactions.":1716,"What happens if I forget to renew my domain?":1717,"If you forget to renew your domain, it typically enters a grace period during which you can renew it at the standard renewal price, but timelines vary by TLD. Failing to renew within that period can result in deletion, auction, or permanent loss. Most domains follow this lifecycle: 1. Expiration Date – The domain stops resolving if not renewed. 2. Grace Renewal Period (often up to 30 days, depending on the registry) – Renewal at regular cost is usually still possible. 3. Redemption Period – The domain may require a higher restoration fee. 4. Pending Delete Period – Final countdown before the domain is released to the public. 5. Public Re-registration – If not purchased, it becomes available to anyone. Some TLDs have shorter timelines or different policies. For investors, expired domains can attract competitive bidding due to traffic history, backlinks, or brandability, increasing reacquisition costs. Enabling auto-renew and maintaining valid payment methods reduces asset loss risk.":1718,"Can I transfer my existing domain to Dynadot?":1719,"Yes, you can transfer your domain to Dynadot! One year is usually added to your domain's expiration date upon transfer, with some exceptions.":1720,"Why is my personal website offline?":1721,"A website can go offline due to DNS misconfiguration, domain expiration, hosting issues, or registry suspension. The cause is usually technical rather than permanent. Common reasons include: DNS Propagation Delay: After updating name servers or DNS records (Domain Name System settings that direct traffic to your hosting server), changes can take 5 minutes to 48 hours to fully propagate globally. Incorrect DNS Records: Mistyped A, AAAA, CNAME, or MX records can prevent resolution. Hosting Configuration Errors: The domain may not be properly linked to your hosting account. Domain Expiration: An expired domain stops resolving until renewed. Registry or Compliance Suspension: Domains may be suspended for policy violations, inaccurate contact data, or abuse reports. If DNS is correctly configured and the domain is active, the issue may be server-side rather than registrar-related. Checking DNS records, expiration status, and hosting configuration typically identifies the root cause. Most top-level domains (TLDs) support privacy protection, but some TLDs don't support privacy protection due to registry restrictions.","If I register a domain, do I have to put my real name/address in Whois?","Yes, accurate registrant information is required when registering a domain. Providing false contact details can violate registration agreements and may lead to suspension or loss of the domain. Whois is the public record of domain ownership information required by ICANN (the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers). However: Most TLDs support domain privacy, which replaces your public contact details with proxy information. The registrar retains your verified real information internally. Privacy does not eliminate legal obligations or prevent court-ordered disclosures. Accurate ownership records are essential for transfers, dispute resolution, and asset verification during resale transactions.","What happens if I forget to renew my domain?","If you forget to renew your domain, it typically enters a grace period during which you can renew it at the standard renewal price, but timelines vary by TLD. Failing to renew within that period can result in deletion, auction, or permanent loss. Most domains follow this lifecycle: 1. Expiration Date – The domain stops resolving if not renewed. 2. Grace Renewal Period (often up to 30 days, depending on the registry) – Renewal at regular cost is usually still possible. 3. Redemption Period – The domain may require a higher restoration fee. 4. Pending Delete Period – Final countdown before the domain is released to the public. 5. Public Re-registration – If not purchased, it becomes available to anyone. Some TLDs have shorter timelines or different policies. For investors, expired domains can attract competitive bidding due to traffic history, backlinks, or brandability, increasing reacquisition costs. Enabling auto-renew and maintaining valid payment methods reduces asset loss risk.","Can I transfer my existing domain to Dynadot?","Yes, you can transfer your domain to Dynadot! Here's how: 1. Start the transfer: Visit our domain transfer page, enter your domain and authorization code, and then click Transfer. The domain is added to your cart and you can proceed to checkout. 3. After completion: You'll receive email updates as the transfer progresses, including confirmation and completion emails. The cause is usually technical rather than permanent. Common reasons include: DNS Propagation Delay: After updating name servers or DNS records (Domain Name System settings that direct traffic to your hosting server), changes can take 5 minutes to 48 hours to fully propagate globally. Incorrect DNS Records: Mistyped A, AAAA, CNAME, or MX records can prevent resolution. Hosting Configuration Errors: The domain may not be properly linked to your hosting account. Domain Expiration: An expired domain stops resolving until renewed. Registry or Compliance Suspension: Domains may be suspended for policy violations, inaccurate contact data, or abuse reports. If DNS is correctly configured and the domain is active, the issue may be server-side rather than registrar-related. Checking DNS records, expiration status, and hosting configuration typically identifies the root cause.
